subject: Problem with plotting two matrices and using a loop

messages.author: dac50c1ae6948875
messages.subject: Problem with plotting two matrices and using a loop
parts:
Hi everyone,
I am trying to "translate" a plot into a ggplot to keep my graphics
consistent, but I am facing some problems and hope somebody can help.
I would like to plot two matrices against each other, like in a
scatterplot. This works easily with plot, for example:
x = matrix(rnorm(100),nrow=10)
y = matrix(rnorm(100),nrow=10)
plot(x,y)
or as well in a loop:
plot(x[1,], y[1,],type="n") # maybe with xlim,ylim argument
for (i in 1:10) {
points(x[i,], y[i,]) }

However, I don't get this to work with ggplot.
Obviously, I cannot just plot the matrices as above like "qplot(x,y)"
as I get an error message, I do not really understand why.
I have tried
xy = data.frame(x,y)
m = ggplot(xy)
m + for (i in 1:10) {
geom_point(data=dafr,aes(x=x[,i],y=y[,i]))
}
But then only the last layer (i=10) of the loop is plotted. If I would
explicitly write all ten loops it works as I want, but my matrices are
actually 160x160, so I would really like to find a better solution.
I have tried something with print() because I've read that it is
needed within loops, but it did not work either.
Any hint would be very much appreciated!

Thanks, Silke.

Have a look at what this code does:

a <- 1
a + for(i in 1:10) {a}

A for loop returns the last value. You want something like:
for (i in 1:10) {

print(m + geom_point(data=xy,aes(x=x[,i],y=y[,i])))
}

Regards,

Hadley

Thank you very much for your response, although the loop did not
really work for me as it returns 10 different plots, one of each
layer, and what I wanted is to have all layers in the same plot.
However I found another solution with the help of a friend:

x = as.numeric(matrix(rnorm(100),nrow=10))
y = as.numeric(matrix(rnorm(100),nrow=10) )

xy = data.frame(x,y)
m = ggplot(xy)

m + geom_point(aes(x=x,y=y))

Seems to be a problem of the data type...

Kind regards,
Silke.

messages.subject: Re: Problem with plotting two matrices and using a loop
parts:
Hi,

If I understand correctly, you can try this:

y <- matrix(rnorm(50*20),ncol=20)

mdf <- data.frame(y)
mdf$x <- seq(1, nrow(y))

qplot(x, value, data=melt(mdf, id="x"), colour= variable , geom="line")

(I replaced 160 by 20 as it was quite slow on my machine)


note that in base graphics you could use matplot(1:50, y, lty=1)


Hope this helps,

baptiste
